title: RBAC v2 observability fallback and SIEM backpressure plan
summary: Proposal for resilient audit evidence export and RBAC v2 graceful-degradation behavior when SIEM ingestion or the evidence pipeline experiences backpressure. Includes schema compatibility notes, prioritization rules, metrics to track, and a staged rollout plan with runbook snippets.
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines how RBAC v2 and the evidence export pipeline should behave when downstream SIEMs or evidence collectors apply backpressure, and what observability signals and fallback behaviors we will implement during rollouts. Goal is to keep product access decisions correct, preserve high-value audit evidence, and avoid cascading failures across the control plane and customer-facing services.

Scope:
- RBAC v2 decision path (policy evaluation, tokens, ephemeral grants)
- Evidence generation (entitlement change events, attestation snapshots, decision logs)
- Evidence transport/export to vendor SIEMs and internal analytics pipelines
- Console and SRE observability for rollout and post-mortem

Problem statement:
We observed two classes of failure during large entitlement churn / infra incidents:
1) Downstream SIEMs rate-limit or drop evidence, causing evidence backlog and memory pressure in the evidence-collector service.
2) Synchronous evidence plumbing (blocking on persistence/export) increases RBAC decision latency or even causes transient denials when buffers fill.
Both outcomes are unacceptable for production SLAs and for customers with strict audit requirements. We need a design that preserves correctness of access control while ensuring evidence exports are resilient and priortized under load.

Design principles:
- Fail-open/closed tradeoffs must favor correctness for high-sensitivity actions (fail-closed for privilege grants; fail-open for low-risk informational reads only after explicit policy).
- Evidence is tiered by value: critical (privilege changes, admin consent, delegation events), important (role assignments, token issuance), best-effort (query logs, read-only resource access). Keep critical evidence durable first.
- Backpressure must be surfaced via signals (metrics, traces, alerts) and handled by bounded queues, sampling, and prioritized throttling rather than by blocking request paths.
- Exports must be schema-versioned and backward-compatible; exporters should annotate events with "export-trace-id" and a compression flag when batching.

Architecture proposal:
1) Decouple decision path from export pipeline
   - RBAC evaluation remains synchronous and writes a compact decision record to a local write-ahead log (WAL) with a durable acknowledgement (fsync or cloud equivalent).
   - Evidence export reads from the WAL asynchronously and is responsible for delivery to downstream systems.

2) Tiered evidence queues and prioritization
   - Maintain 3 logical queues per tenant: critical, important, best-effort. Each queue has bounded capacity and separate retry/backoff policies.
   - Admission controller enforces memory limits and rejects or samples lower tiers when under pressure.
   - Critical queue uses synchronous replication to persistent store and immediate enqueue for export; exports from critical queue get higher concurrency.

3) Backpressure handling strategies
   - Short-circuit: When exporter sees sustained downstream 429/503s from SIEM, mark exporter in backpressure state and switch to local disk-backed batching.
   - Priority shed: Drop or sample best-effort events deterministically (e.g., 1:1000 sample) while preserving critical and important tiers intact. Sampling policy is configurable per-tenant.
   - Graceful degrade: For request paths that currently wait on evidence persistence, we will switch them to an asynchronous acceptance model. The response to the caller will include a lightweight evidence-hash and an eventual-delivery token for tracing.
   - Circuit breaker: Exporter-level circuit breaker that notifies the router to slow down non-critical traffic or route to secondary export endpoints (replica SIEMs).

4) SIEM export backoff and multi-destination routing
   - Exports include diagnosis headers (schema version, batch size, compression, tenant-id). On persistent errors, route to a secondary ingest endpoint (if configured) or to an internal long-term archive (S3).
   - Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries; cap total retries and escalate to PagerDuty for critical exports exceeding a threshold.

5) Schema and evidence compatibility
   - Add a minimal envelope: {"v":"2.1","tier":"critical|important|best_effort","event_id":"...","payload":"...","sign":"..."}. Envelope fields are required; payload is an opaque JSON blob for consumers that opt-in to parsing.
   - Maintain strict backward compatibility for field names used by existing SIEM parsers for at least two major versions; provide a translator lambda to convert 2.x -> 1.x for legacy consumers.

Operational signals (metrics & alerts):
- Per-tenant queue depth by tier (gauge)
- Exporter 5xx/429 rate and consecutive error streak
- Ratio of dropped/sampled events by tier (counter)
- Average decision latency P50/P95 when export is queued vs when sync persistence succeed (histogram)
- Evidence backlog age distribution (how long oldest event has been pending)
- Disk-backed-batch size and time-to-first-ship
- SIEM downstream throttle alerts: trigger when exporter sees >1% of requests returning 429 for 5m

Runbook snippets (for SRE / security ops):
- Detect: Alert on exporter 429 spike or persistent increase in critical-queue aged events > 10 minutes.
- Triage: Verify downstream SIEM health (network, certs, ingestion limits). If SIEM healthy but rate-limiting, enable accelerated S3-archive fallback and notify CS for impacted tenants.
- Mitigate: Temporarily increase export parallelism for critical queue (config flag), reduce sampling on important tier, disable best-effort flows.
- Restore: Drain backlog to < 1 minute age and set exporter to normal mode. Re-run replay for archived batches if needed.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests: queue eviction, sampling determinism, envelope compatibility conversions.
- Integration tests: simulated SIEM 429/500 and verify tiered behavior and that decision latency stays within SLOs.
- Chaos test: inject random exporter failures in staging and assert no RBAC decision paths fail closed unexpectedly.
- Canary rollout: 3-phase
   1) Internal canary: 2% of infra tenants, enable observability flags and disk-backed-batch mode.
   2) Beta customers: opt-in list of 3 enterprise tenants for 2 weeks. Monitor metrics and collect feedback.
   3) Global: 100% with default safe sampling (preserve critical events) and auto-fallback enabled.

Metrics to validate during canary:
- Decision latency P95 not exceeding baseline + 10ms for non-admin paths
- No more than 0.1% of critical events dropped or delayed > 1 minute
- Exporter error rate stable or falling after retries/backoff policies

Open questions / policy decisions:
- What exact list of events are classified as "critical"? Propose: any change to role bindings, grant/deny overrides, delegation-of-authority, key rotations. Need security leadership sign-off.
- Tenant-level sampling defaults: conservative vs aggressive by default? Recommend conservative (sample low) and allow tenant opt-in to higher sampling for debugging.
- Retention and replay window for archived batches: 30 days default, configurable.

Action items:
- [Anika] Draft API changes for evidence envelope and publish schema RFC (target 2025-02-19).
- [Mateo] Spike: disk-backed-batch prototype and perf test (2025-02-26).
- [Priya] Update RBAC evaluation path to write to WAL and emit evidence-hash (2025-03-05).
- [Jun] Wire exporter metrics and alerts into Console dashboards (2025-03-10).
- [Lena] Coordinate security review and enterprise CS communication (2025-03-12).

Appendix: example event envelope (human-readable)
- v: 2.1
- tier: critical
- event_id: sec-20250212-0001
- timestamp: 2025-02-12T14:33:21Z
- payload: {"action":"role.bind","actor":"alice@redwood.ai","target":"project:payments:role:admin","diff":{...}}
- sign: sha256-signed-by-kms

Notes on uniqueness: this doc emphasizes exporter-level backpressure strategies, explicit tiering of evidence, disk-backed local batching as a first-class fallback, and a canary progression that tests for decision-path latency regressions while preserving critical evidence. It is intentionally prescriptive on operational signals and runbook steps to make the rollout reproducible by SRE/security teams.

If you have suggested edits to event classification or want to add tenant-specific overrides to sampling, please comment inline or raise SEC-1298.
